references.text: The parallel text in Exodus where the same command against making carved images is given, with almost identical wording about images of what is in heaven, on earth, or in the water.
The prohibition against making cast idols, which expands on the ban against idolatry.
Repeats the prohibition against turning to idols and against making cast idols.
Prohibition against setting up idols, carved images, or stone pillars in the land.
Moses warns against making carved images in the form of man, woman, animal, bird, creeping thing, or fish.
A curse is pronounced on anyone who makes a carved or cast image, an abomination to the Lord.
Isaiah mocks those who make idols and carved images that cannot help.
Paul speaks to the Athenians about how we should not think of the divine as being like gold, silver, or stone, shaped by human art and thought.
Paul describes how people exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images resembling mortal man, birds, four-footed animals, and creeping things.
